indexEyebrow: Kindergarten and Grade 1 · Learning to read
indexLead: Little books for children who are learning to read. Each book is one sheet of paper, folded into a cover and three pages. The decodable readers follow a phonics scope and sequence, one set at a time; the picture readers are written to be about Levels A to C.
kindDecodableText: Every word in a decodable reader can be sounded out with the letter sounds the class has learned so far, or is a heart word the class has already learned. The text pages have no pictures: the child reads each sentence and draws it. The drawing shows whether the child understood the sentence, and no picture gives a word away.
kindPictureText: Picture readers, about Levels A to C, have one clear picture on each page and a short sentence of sight words, words the child can sound out, and the word the picture shows. Before reading, name the pictures with the child and read the book's new words together (never more than three). Then the child reads, pointing under each word.
setsLead: Each set adds a few letter sounds and heart words. A book in a set uses only the sounds and heart words of that set and the sets before it.
levelsLead: Levels A, B, and C are the first guided reading levels. Our books are written to approximate these levels, so choose by what you know about each reader.
foldTitle: How to print and fold a mini-book
fold1: Print the mini-book page on one sheet of paper.
fold3: Fold the left half back. The cover is now in front, pages 2 and 3 are inside, and page 4 is on the back.
howDecodable1: Before reading, practice the book's new sounds and warm-up words together and read its heart words.
howDecodable2: The child reads each page aloud, sounding out the words, then draws what the sentence says.
howDecodable3: Then use the Read and Talk page: the child rereads the text in large print, sounds out the words in the "Sound these out" box, reads the heart words, and talks about the questions with you.
howPicture1: Before reading, name the pictures with the child and read the new words together.
howPicture2: The child reads each page, pointing under each word. If the child says a word that fits the picture but not the print, such as "lamb" for "sheep," point to the first letter: "Could this be lamb? What letter would lamb start with?"
howPicture3: Then use the Read and Talk page: read the book again and talk about the questions.
talkText: Every book comes with a second sheet, Read and Talk: the whole text again in large print, the book's word lists, two or three questions to talk about after reading, and a note for the teacher. Each time the child rereads the book, they check an "I read it" box.
printNote: Each book opens on its own page, where you can print it. Without a paid plan, the number of pages you can print is limited.
setLead: Little books for children who know the sounds of Sets {range}. Every word can be sounded out with those sounds or is a heart word taught in Set {n} or earlier.
setLeadFirst: Little books for the first letter sounds a class learns. Every word can be sounded out with these sounds or is one of the set's heart words.
setBefore: The books also use the letter sounds and heart words of the sets before: {list}.
levelLeadA: Little books about Level A: one short line on each page, one clear picture, and a sentence pattern that repeats or changes only a little.
levelLeadB: Little books about Level B: a little more text on each page and a sentence pattern that changes, often on the last page, so the child has to read every word.
levelLeadC: Little books about Level C: little stories and fact books, some pages with two sentences and no pattern to lean on.
